verses.text: When Rachel saw that she was not having any children for Jacob, she became jealous of her sister. She said to Jacob, "Give me children, or I will die!"
Jacob became angry with her and said, "Am I God? He is the one who has kept you from having children."
Then she said, "Here is my slave woman Bilhah. Sleep with her, so that she can have children for me. Then I too can have a family through her."
So she gave him her slave woman Bilhah as a wife, and Jacob slept with her.
Bilhah became pregnant and gave Jacob a son.
Then Rachel said, "God has judged in my favour. He has listened to me and given me a son." So she named him Dan, which means "he judged".
Rachel's slave woman Bilhah became pregnant again and gave Jacob a second son.
Then Rachel said, "I have had a great struggle with my sister, and I have won." So she named him Naphtali, which means "my struggle".
When Leah saw that she had stopped having children, she took her slave woman Zilpah and gave her to Jacob as a wife.
Leah's slave woman Zilpah gave Jacob a son.
Then Leah said, "What good fortune!" So she named him Gad, which means "good fortune".
Leah's slave woman Zilpah gave Jacob a second son.
Then Leah said, "How happy I am! The women will call me happy." So she named him Asher, which means "happy".

During the wheat harvest, Reuben went out into the fields and found some mandrake plants, which were believed to help women have children. He brought them to his mother Leah. Rachel said to Leah, "Please give me some of your son's mandrakes."

But Leah said to her, "Was it not enough that you took away my husband? Will you take my son's mandrakes too?" "Very well," Rachel said, "he can sleep with you tonight in return for your son's mandrakes."
When Jacob came in from the fields that evening, Leah went out to meet him. "You must sleep with me tonight," she said. "I have paid for you with my son's mandrakes." So he slept with her that night.
God listened to Leah, and she became pregnant and gave Jacob a fifth son.
Then Leah said, "God has rewarded me for giving my slave woman to my husband." So she named him Issachar, which sounds like "reward".
Leah became pregnant again and gave Jacob a sixth son.
Then Leah said, "God has given me a precious gift. This time my husband will honour me, because I have given him six sons." So she named him Zebulun, which sounds like "honour".
Some time later she gave birth to a daughter and named her Dinah.
Then God remembered Rachel. He listened to her and made it possible for her to have children.
She became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She said, "God has taken away my shame."
She named him Joseph, which means "may he add", and said, "May the LORD add another son to me."
After Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, "Let me go, so that I can go back to my own home and country.
Give me my wives and children, for whom I have worked for you, and I will be on my way. You know how much work I have done for you."
But Laban said to him, "If you are pleased with me, please stay. I have learned by signs that the LORD has blessed me because of you."
He added, "Tell me what you want to be paid, and I will pay it."
Jacob said to him, "You know how I have worked for you, and how well your livestock has done under my care.
You had very little before I came, and it has grown into a great deal. The LORD has blessed you wherever I have gone. But now, when can I do something for my own family?"
"What shall I give you?" Laban asked. "Do not give me anything," Jacob replied. "But if you will do this one thing for me, I will go on looking after your flocks and caring for them.
Let me go through all your flocks today and take out every speckled or spotted sheep, every dark-coloured lamb, and every spotted or speckled goat. They will be my pay.

In the future my honesty will speak for me. Whenever you check on the animals you have paid me, any goat that is not speckled or spotted, and any lamb that is not dark-coloured, will count as stolen if it is found with me."
"Agreed," said Laban. "Let it be as you have said."

But that same day Laban removed all the male goats that had stripes or spots, all the speckled or spotted female goats, all that had white on them, and all the dark-coloured lambs. He put them in the care of his sons.
Then he put a distance of three days' journey between himself and Jacob, while Jacob went on looking after the rest of Laban's flocks.
Jacob took fresh-cut branches from poplar, almond and plane trees. He peeled white stripes on them by stripping off the bark and showing the white wood underneath.
Then he put the peeled branches in all the water troughs, so that they were right in front of the flocks when they came to drink. The animals mated when they came to drink.
They mated in front of the branches, and they gave birth to young that were striped or speckled or spotted.

Jacob set apart the young animals of the flock by themselves. He made the rest face the striped and dark-coloured animals that belonged to Laban. So he built up his own flocks and kept them separate from Laban's animals.
Whenever the stronger animals were mating, Jacob put the branches in the troughs in front of them, so that they would mate near the branches.
But if the animals were weak, he did not put the branches there. So the weak animals went to Laban, and the strong ones to Jacob.
In this way Jacob became very rich. He had large flocks, male and female servants, and camels and donkeys.
